headline: Planting virtual trees around Ann Arbor
intro: Ann Arbor Go is a phone game where players explore a map, plant virtual trees on nearby surfaces, and defend them from squirrels with acorns. Maxwell Zuber and I built it for our XR course.
context: University of Michigan · XR course project · Oct 2022
role: I worked on the mode and navigation controls, camera setup, and acorn interactions. Maxwell and I shared the implementation, with both of us working across the game.

hero.alt: An illustrated map-exploration scene and phone AR scene connected by shared inventory and planted-tree state.
hero.caption: A diagram of the two scenes, based on the original C# code. The linked team video shows the mobile game.
hero.credit: Original project: Le Qin and Maxwell Zuber

metrics.label: test device
metrics.note: Development used both the Unity Editor and the device

question.title: Moving between the map and the camera
question.text: The game has separate scenes for exploring the map and interacting in AR. Inventory and planted-tree information carry between them so players can switch modes and keep playing.

steps.title: Explore the area
steps.text: Compass and landmark cues help players find their way around the map. Maxwell proposed a drone mode for scouting before traveling.

steps.title: Plant a tree
steps.text: In the camera view, the AR cursor marks where a seed will go on a detected surface.

steps.title: Defend it from squirrels
steps.text: Players use acorns as projectiles and manage items through the inventory and shop controls.

finding.title: Movement felt different on the phone
finding.text: Problems deploying to the iPhone delayed our device tests. Once we could test it, movement that had felt fast in the Unity Editor felt slow on the phone. We needed regular device tests to catch those differences during development.

details: The original is a single-player game built by two teammates. Its shared state connects scenes within one game; it doesn't synchronize multiple players.

The browser demo uses a generated park and simplified planting controls. Its water and boost actions and growth stages differ from the mobile game. The original deployable mobile build hasn't been recovered.
credits: Built with Unity, C#, AR Foundation, and Mapbox. The original team recording remains linked below.
The project source, commit history, and my course postmortem document the work described here.
